Put the phone on your hitting-arm side. That's your right if you're right-handed, and your left if you're left-handed.

Line it up with the baseline.
Stand the phone outside the court, in line with the baseline, 2 to 3 big steps outside the outer sideline. Between two courts, halfway across is usually right. Point the camera straight along the baseline at where you serve, so the line runs up the middle of the screen.
3
Chest height, and level.
Set the phone about 1.3 to 1.6 m high, around chest height. Keep it level. Don't tilt it up at the sky. The level guide turns solid when it's right.
4
Upright, standard lens.
Stand the phone upright, with the camera facing your serving spot. Use the standard 1x lens and don't zoom.
5
Check the sun.
Stand at your serving spot and look at the phone. The sun should be behind the phone or off to one side, not behind you. If you're squinting a little, that's good: the camera isn't.

Stand tall, then toss.
Walk to your spot and stand tall for two seconds. Then toss a ball as you would for a serve and catch it. We'll check you, your toss and the light, and tell you if anything needs to move.

Privacy

Serve Coach analyses your videos on this phone. There is no account, and the app sends nothing to us or anyone else.

Your videos, stats, key frames, logs and profile are stored only on this phone. Comfort answers are stored only if you say yes, and are never exported unless you choose.

Pose tracking uses Google’s MediaPipe, bundled inside the app. Its usage reporting is blocked, so it cannot send anything either.

You can export everything as JSON or CSV, and delete a session, all videos or everything, in Profile → Storage and privacy.

The full privacy policy will be published before the public release.

How we coach

Cues and drills are coaching practice, not proven by trials for players like you.

Serve Coach is independent. It isn't affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by any coach or coaching business we cite. Names appear only to cite published coaching material.

Serve Coach is not a medical service. If something hurts, see a GP, physiotherapist or sports doctor.

What it is

Am I driving into the court?

How far into the court your front foot lands, measured from your start position.

How we measure it
We find your front toe at the start.

How sure we are

Tested on simulated serves and not accurate enough yet, so it stays experimental. Not yet checked on real courts.

At the recommended set-ups (11 simulated serves filmed 7 to 9 m away), the typical error was about 6 cm, and 1 in 20 serves was off by about 24 cm or more.

Our stated range held the true value on 10 of 11 of those serves.

Our pass mark is a typical error within 8 cm, and 1 in 20 serves within 15 cm. It hasn't passed yet.

Most serves were close, but a few were well off, mostly with the phone sideways at the fence, 9 m away.

Test details
Known limits
Heights and distances depend on your entered height, so the whole set could sit a few centimetres high or low. Comparisons with your own serves are sharper than the absolute numbers.
Body tracking from phone video is noisier than lab systems, and left and right can swap. We assign sides from the shape of the serve.
There are no published landing distances for club players, so this is shown as your own trend only.
Every check so far used computer-generated serves: one simulated player on a rendered court, filmed by our own model of a phone camera. Real players, phones, courts and court lights may do worse.
Compared with your own serves

We compare this only with your own usual serves. Published trunk angles and professional leg values measure different things, so we don't show them.
